games.thirdReasoning: Denver's six-game win streak, a deep and varied pass rush, and a clean quarterback situation line up against a Pittsburgh team that just benched its big free-agent QB signing, is already missing its starting left guard and top edge rusher, and managed only 49 first-half rushing yards combined over its last two games — that's more structural disadvantage than a 3.5-point number fully prices in. The most surprising finding was the market tightening toward Pittsburgh (Broncos -4.5 to -3.5) right as the Rudolph news broke, which argues some money sees value on the Steelers; weighing that against the O-line mismatch and Rudolph's near-zero live reps, I still lean Denver to cover. A surprisingly sharp Rudolph debut or a short week sapping Denver's own execution would be what flips this.
thirdResearch: [angle] Steelers released/benched Aaron Rodgers on Nov. 25 and officially named Mason Rudolph their Week 12 starter, ending the Rodgers era with the team at 6-4 — a locker-room shakeup two days before a national Friday broadcast. (Yahoo Sports, Nov 26, 2026; favors Broncos — unsettled QB room.)

[angle] A day before the switch, head coach Mike McCarthy publicly said Rodgers 'is our quarterback,' then reversed course less than 24 hours later — a sudden shift suggesting real internal disagreement about the move. (Washington Post, Nov 26, 2026; favors Broncos — organizational uncertainty.)

Mason Rudolph is a 7-year veteran with only 19 career starts (9-9-1 record) and had thrown just 1-of-4 passes all season in mop-up duty before tonight — he's walking into a pressure spot with almost no live 2026 reps. (CBS Sports gametracker preview, Nov 27, 2026; favors Broncos.)

Steelers starting left guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a significant ankle injury vs. Cincinnati on Nov. 15, is on IR and out again tonight, with Spencer Anderson replacing him for a third straight game. (CBS Sports preview via AP / ClutchPoints, Nov 2026; favors Broncos — patchwork O-line.)

Steelers starting edge rusher opposite T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith, was ruled OUT with an ankle injury after missing the entire practice week; Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer fill in. (RotoWire, Nov 26, 2026; favors Broncos — weakens Pittsburgh's own pass rush on Rudolph's night and reduces pressure on Nix.)

Denver has 5 different players with 3-plus sacks this season, and the Steelers O-line — already down McCormick — allowed 5 sacks to Philadelphia last week. That's a bad matchup for a shuffled line protecting a QB with almost no live reps. (CBS Sports preview via AP, Nov 27, 2026; favors Broncos.)

Pittsburgh's running game has totaled just 49 rushing yards combined in the first halves of its last two games, so Rudolph won't have a steady run-game crutch behind that same shuffled line. (CBS Sports preview via AP, Nov 27, 2026; favors Broncos.)

[angle] Denver has won 6 straight games and sits 9-2, controlling the AFC West and chasing its first division title and top playoff seed in a decade — real, documented motivation to keep the streak alive on national TV. (Fox Sports, 'Broncos facing brutal stretch run,' Nov 2026; favors Broncos.)

[angle] Denver rookie RB Jonah Coleman ran for 111 yards and 3 TDs last week after starter JK Dobbins was suspended for conduct detrimental to the team — the suspension hasn't actually hurt Denver's offense. (CBS Sports preview via AP, Nov 27, 2026; neutral-to-favors Broncos — turned a potential negative into a non-issue.)

[Spread] Despite the QB chaos, the spread reportedly shrank from Broncos -4.5 toward Broncos -3.5 (AP's 'Broncos by 3 1/2' as of game day) rather than growing — a mild reverse-line move toward Pittsburgh that the public QB-change narrative alone doesn't fully explain. (CBS Sports preview via AP / oddsindex.com, Nov 27, 2026; favors Steelers on the number.)

[Spread] Pittsburgh is 5-2 against the spread this season and 1-1 ATS as an underdog — a team that has covered more often than not even while losing straight-up recently. (StatMuse, Nov 2026; favors Steelers' cover profile.)

[Spread] This is Pittsburgh's first Friday game since 1946 and Denver's first since 1985 — a historically rare short-week scheduling quirk that cuts against both teams' normal preparation equally, tempering how much extra credit either side's 'short week' deserves. (CBS Sports preview via AP, Nov 27, 2026; neutral.)

Kickoff weather in Pittsburgh is forecast in the mid-40s and breezy with a chance of a brief shower — not extreme, but one more small variable for a Denver team that rarely deals with late-fall East Coast dampness, versus a Steelers team that plays home games in it every year.
